links.outcome: Model accuracy after swapping corneal region backgrounds (cut-and-paste perturbation)
links.effect: Accuracy was highly dependent on background context for certain diseases; accuracy for infectious keratitis and acute primary angle closure dropped significantly after background alteration.
links.quote: Cut-and-paste validation demonstrated that model accuracy was highly dependent on the background context for certain diseases; for instance, the accuracy for infectious keratitis and acute primary angle closure dropped significantly upon background alteration.

links.outcome: Fidelity of Grad-CAM++ attention maps to expert lesion annotations (IoU) by prediction correctness
links.effect: IoU of attention maps against expert annotations was significantly higher for correct than for incorrect predictions, linking visual explanation to diagnostic reliability.
links.quote: Critically, the clinical relevance of the attention maps measured by the IoU against expert annotations was significantly higher for correct predictions than for incorrect predictions, linking the model's visual explanation to its diagnostic reliability.

screen.reason: The study evaluates an existing YOLOv5 model using explainability maps and stress-testing/perturbation validation (cut-and-paste background perturbation) to audit reliance on spurious extracorneal background features versus true lesion areas.

primary.practice: explainability and perturbation-based validation (Grad-CAM++ and cut-and-paste testing)
